record.title: European Commission opens consultation on revised DSA election-risk guidelines for AI and information manipulation
record.summary: On 10 November 2026, the European Commission opened a consultation on draft revised DSA guidelines for very large online platforms and search engines addressing systemic risks to electoral processes, including generative AI and information manipulation. The Commission’s consultation page summarizes proposals for earlier response to coordinated inauthentic behavior, pre-election recommender manipulation tests and six-month change records, persistent labels for AI-generated deepfakes, rapid removal of illegal candidate deepfakes, candidate protection channels and public post-election reports. Its linked draft PDF failed to load in the available reader, so this summary follows the Commission’s page rather than uninspected clause text. The guidance remains a consultation draft; adoption, implementation and election-integrity effects are not established.
organizations: Directorate-General for Communications Networks, Content and Technology

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The European Commission published a consultation on draft revised Digital Services Act election-risk guidelines on 10 November 2026; the consultation closes on 23 November 2026.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The Commission’s consultation page says the draft proposes earlier detection and disruption of coordinated inauthentic behavior; recommender-system manipulation tests before each national election and records of changes made in the six months before a vote; persistent labels on AI-generated deepfakes and rapid removal of illegal candidate deepfakes; candidate support channels; and public post-election mitigation reports within 30 days.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The Commission’s April 2024 guidance addressed providers’ existing DSA Article 35 obligations to take reasonable, proportionate and effective measures against election-related systemic risks.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The draft is under consultation and is not shown here as adopted or binding; platform implementation and effects on election integrity have not been measured. The linked draft PDF could not be inspected in the available reader, so the exact proposal wording and full changes from 2024 remain unverified.

evidence_gaps.description: The linked draft guidelines could not be inspected because the official download failed with a Unicode decoding error.
The full draft has not been compared clause by clause with the April 2024 guidance and DSA Article 35 obligations.
No adoption, platform implementation or measured effect on election integrity was established.

brief.importance_rationale: If adopted and applied as proposed, revised DSA election guidance could materially change how very large platforms and search engines detect manipulation, test recommender systems, label AI-generated deepfakes and report election-risk mitigation. The current item is a consultation draft, not a binding new duty or measured outcome.
limitations: The official linked draft PDF returned a Unicode decoding error in the available reader; the account relies on the Commission’s summary page.
The proposal is in consultation and is not evidence of new binding duties, platform compliance, or election-integrity outcomes.
The exact relationship between each proposed measure and the 2024 guidance is not fully resolved without the draft text.

brief.title: European Commission opens consultation on revised DSA election-risk guidelines for AI and information manipulation
brief.why_it_matters: The proposal would make electoral-risk mitigation more specific for very large platforms and search engines, including recommender-system testing and operational duties around AI-generated content. Its status and effects remain open: the Commission has published a consultation draft, not evidence of adoption or compliance.
